name: Marché Central
description: The beating heart of downtown Yaoundé. Narrow aisles packed with fabric, spices, shoes and fresh produce — go early, haggle politely, and bring cash.

name: Marché Mokolo
description: Cameroon's biggest market by volume of goods. Electronics, wax-print fabric, spare parts — if it exists, someone at Mokolo sells it.

name: Mont Fébé
description: A forested hill overlooking the city with the best sunrise view in Yaoundé. A short hike or a drive up rewards you with a full skyline panorama.

name: Musée National du Cameroun
description: Housed in a former presidential palace, this museum traces Cameroon's kingdoms, colonial history and independence through masks, thrones and archives.

name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame des Victoires
description: A calm, twin-towered landmark in the middle of the busy centre-ville — step inside for stained glass and a moment of quiet away from the traffic.

name: Jardin Botanique et Zoologique de Mvog-Betsi
description: A shaded rescue-animal sanctuary and botanical walk — gorillas, chimpanzees and native trees, run by a conservation NGO right inside the city.

name: Stade Ahmadou Ahidjo
description: The historic home of the Indomitable Lions. On match day the whole neighborhood turns into one long celebration before kickoff even starts.

name: Lac Municipal
description: A small lakeside park popular with families on Sunday afternoons — paddle boats, grilled fish stalls, and shaded benches along the water.

name: Quartier Bastos
description: The diplomatic quarter — leafy avenues, embassies, and a growing strip of restaurants and cafés perfect for an evening walk.

name: Monument de la Réunification
description: A sweeping concrete spiral monument marking the 1961 reunification of Cameroon — climb to the top for one of the best free skyline views downtown.

name: Village Artisanal du Mfoundi
description: A cluster of artisan workshops where you can watch wood carvers, bronze casters and weavers work, then buy directly from the maker.

name: Chutes de la Méfou
description: A short drive outside the city, these forest waterfalls are a favorite weekend escape for Yaoundéans who want fresh air and running water.

name: Musée Blackitude
description: A striking pan-African art museum celebrating the diaspora's contribution to global culture, with rotating exhibitions and a sculpture garden.

name: Complexe Sportif de Mfandena
description: A neighborhood sports ground where locals gather every evening for pick-up football, basketball and running — a great way to meet people.

name: Marché des Fleurs de Nlongkak
description: A small, colourful flower and plant market tucked into a roundabout — a favorite stop for anyone decorating for a wedding or naming ceremony.

name: Palais des Congrès
description: A landmark of late-70s Cameroonian architecture, still used for state ceremonies and major conferences — an impressive photo stop on the ring road.

name: Université de Yaoundé I
description: Cameroon's oldest and largest public university, spread across a leafy hillside campus in Ngoa-Ekelle — walk through and you'll feel the energy of thousands of students between lectures.

name: Université de Yaoundé II
description: Cameroon's law, economics and journalism powerhouse, set on a newer campus just outside the city in Soa — home to ESSTIC and IRIC, two of the country's most competitive schools.

name: École Normale Supérieure de Yaoundé
description: The country's flagship teacher-training college, right next to Université de Yaoundé I — generations of Cameroon's teachers trained on this campus.

name: Lycée Général Leclerc
description: One of Cameroon's most prestigious public high schools, with alumni across the country's government and business world — a proud landmark for the whole neighborhood.

name: Canal Olympia Yaoundé
description: A modern cinema and live-event hall that also hosts concerts and community screenings — the go-to spot for a night out watching the latest releases.

name: Restaurant Le Bantoo
description: A relaxed Bastos favorite for Cameroonian classics done well — ndolé, grilled fish and plantain, with a shaded terrace that fills up fast on weekend evenings.

name: Restaurant Saveurs d'Asie
description: A long-running Asian kitchen popular with Yaoundé's expat and student crowd alike — good for a change of pace from the city's grills and stews.

name: Santa Lucia Supermarket
description: A well-stocked supermarket in the diplomatic quarter, popular for imported goods that are harder to find elsewhere in the city.

name: Casino Supermarket Warda
description: Part of the busy Carrefour Warda commercial strip — a reliable one-stop supermarket for groceries and household goods.

name: Centre Commercial Dovv
description: One of Yaoundé's larger shopping centers, with a supermarket anchor plus smaller boutiques — a good stop for a full errand run in one trip.

name: Stade Militaire de Yaoundé
description: A community sports ground used for local football matches and military ceremonies alike — smaller and friendlier than the big stadium downtown.

name: Hôtel Hilton Yaoundé
description: A landmark high-rise hotel in the heart of downtown, with a rooftop pool and skyline views — a popular meeting point even for people not staying there.

name: Institut Français du Cameroun
description: A cultural center with a cinema, library, theatre and regular exhibitions — one of the best places to catch live music, film screenings, or a gallery opening.

name: Marché Essos
description: A busy neighborhood market east of downtown, known for fresh produce and some of the best street food stalls in the city.

name: Quartier Mvog-Mbi
description: A dense, lively commercial quarter south of downtown, packed with small shops, bars and grilled-fish spots — a good taste of everyday Yaoundé life.

name: École Nationale Supérieure Polytechnique
description: Cameroon's top engineering school, tucked into the same Ngoa-Ekelle university district as UY1 — famously competitive to get into.

name: Basilique Marie-Reine-des-Apôtres
description: A striking minor basilica on the hill of Mvolyé, the mother parish of the Archdiocese of Yaoundé — its terrace also gives one of the city's best southward views.

name: Colline de Mvolyé
description: The hill that gives the Basilique its perch — a quiet climb rewarded with sweeping views over the southern half of the city.

name: Carrefour Warda
description: A buzzing commercial crossroads with shops, supermarkets and street food side by side — one of the city's busiest everyday meeting points.

name: Marché Nkolndongo
description: A neighborhood market on the city's southern edge, less crowded than the big central markets and popular with locals for everyday shopping.
